LEGACY_D_GATE_DEFINITION.name: RELATIVE_LOCALIZATION
LEGACY_D_GATE_DEFINITION.statistic: fraction of in-window frames with r80_organiser <= bound

DECOMPOSITION.ABSOLUTE_LOCALIZATION_RESULT: the cloud radius stays under an absolute ceiling in the overwhelming majority of frames on every healthy arm at both L: observed fractions D/seed9501=1.0000, D/seed9502=0.9333, D/seed9503=0.9333, P/seed9101=0.2778, P/seed9102=0.9722, P/seed9103=0.9833, P/seed9104=0.9722, P/seed9105=0.9944, P/seed9106=1.0000
DECOMPOSITION.WHY: the two questions coincide only if the threshold scales with L; here it does not over 36 -> 72, so a FAIL of this gate is evidence about an absolute radius ceiling and its tail, not about the L-dependence of the radius.

REASONS: THRESHOLD_ESSENTIALLY_INDEPENDENT_OF_L: bound(36)=12.60, bound(72)=12.80, ratio 1.0159. Over the only two domain sizes used by OBTC02 the absolute term 12.8 is binding at L=36 (0.35*36=12.6) and binding at L=72 (0.35*72=25.2>12.8), so doubling L changes the admissible radius by 1.6%. The gate therefore tests an ABSOLUTE radius, not its dependence on L.

NO_CROSS_DOMAIN_COMPARISON: RELATIVE_LOCALIZATION is evaluated inside a single arm and never forms a ratio, difference or regression across L. Domain invariance is a statement about how a quantity varies with L; a per-arm threshold cannot express it.

REDUNDANT_WITH_P: the identical condition, identical statistic and identical binding threshold are already applied to the five passing P arms at L=36. The D arms add no new inferential content beyond re-running the same absolute test on a larger torus.

HIGH_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RATE_AT_L=72: under data generated by the frozen LawSpec (so H-bound is true by construction) the gate fails with probability 0.407 at L=72 versus 0.030 at L=36. The asymmetry is not physical: it comes from the heavier upper tail of r80_organiser once periodic images stop truncating it.

ANTI_CONSISTENCY_AT_L=72: as the number of frames grows the failure probability FALLS at L=36 (60 -> 0.0623, 180 -> 0.0312, 540 -> 0.0043, 1800 -> 0.0001) but RISES at L=72 (60 -> 0.2992, 180 -> 0.4110, 540 -> 0.5073, 1800 -> 0.6163). A well-posed test of a true hypothesis converges to acceptance. At L=72 the true frame-wise exceedance probability sits above the 5% budget, so more evidence makes rejection more certain: the criterion is anti-consistent there, and the amount of data — not the physics — decides the verdict.

A_DIRECT_MEASURE_DISAGREES: the quantity the axis is about — the cloud-frame radius r80, measured from the cloud's own centre and so free of the organiser-frame offset — has median-of-arm-medians 7.0711 at L=36 and 7.0355 at L=72, a relative difference of 0.0050 (0.50%), while the legacy gate reports FAIL on two of three D arms.
NOTE: This is an append-only reinterpretation of an already-frozen result. The OBTC02 disposition, its D-axis verdict and its frozen thresholds are NOT modified, NOT relaxed and NOT recomputed. Nothing here converts an OBTC02 FAIL into a PASS.
WHAT_THIS_STATUS_DOES_NOT_LICENCE: it does not establish that the cloud is bounded as L grows — that is exactly what OBDI01 must test with fresh pre-registered data
it does not remove the legacy gate: §16 keeps it as a locked secondary endpoint
it does not re-score any OBTC02 arm
